chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, who said:

I was with Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) in what is between Mecca and Medina. When he turned to his left, there was a black, beastly dog. He said: 'What is the matter with you? May Allah make you ugly, how fierce is your rushing!' And it was resembling a bird. I said: 'What is this? May I be sacrificed for you.' He said: 'This is Gusaym, the postman of the Jinn. Hisham died at this moment, and he (Gusaym) flies, announcing it in every city.'

key_terms.بَرِيدُ الْجِنِّ: Postman of the Jinn, referring to the role of conveying news among Jinn
key_terms.بَلْدَةٍ: City or town, indicating the scope of the announcement
key_terms.غُثَيْمٌ: Gusaym, a specific name for the Jinn postman mentioned in the hadith
key_terms.هِشَامٌ: Hisham, the Jinn whose death was being announced

ai.seo_question: Who is Gusaym the postman of the Jinn in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi’s chapter on dogs illustrates the Shia cosmological view of the unseen world, where Jinn possess physical forms and social structures akin to humans. Abu Hamza al-Thumali’s direct observation of Gusaym, the Jinn postman, announcing Hisham’s death across cities highlights the belief in instantaneous communication among the Jinn, a concept often linked to their ability to ascend to the lower heavens. This narrative serves as a practical example of how the Imams interpreted natural phenomena through the lens of the unseen (ghayb).

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Maalik Bin Atiyya, from Abu Hamza Al Sumaly who said,

‘I was with Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> in what is between Makkah and Al-Medina, when he<sup>asws</sup> turned to his<sup>asws</sup> left, so there was an entirely black dog. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What is the matter with you? Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Made you ugly, how fiercely you rush! and it was the resemblance of a bird’. So I said, ‘What is this? May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This is Gusaym, a postman of the Jinn. Hisham died at this time, and he (turned himself into) a bird notifying it in every city’.
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Malik ibn ‘Atiyyah from abu Hamzah al-Thumaliy who has said the following:

“Once I was with abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, on the road between Makkah and al-Madinah and I saw on his left side a dog of one color, all black. He (the Imam) said, ‘What is the matter with you, may Allah disfigure you, how fiercely you rush!’ It then resembled a bird. I then asked, ‘What is this? I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It was Ghuthaym, mailman of Jinn. Hisham has died in this hour and it flies to spread this news in every town.’”
